title: Shadow IT: Why It Happens, Why It's Risky, and How DLP Can Help
summary: Shadow IT puts your data at risk when employees bypass IT. Learn why it happens, real-world examples, and a 3-step plan to fix it.
body_text: Shadow IT. Sounds scary, right? But what if the really scary thing was the root cause behind people using unauthorized devices, apps, or software: slow approval workflows? Shadow IT is what happens when company processes move slower than the actual pace of work. Employees aren't trying to break the rules; they're only trying to hit a deadline, close a deal, or share a file that's too big for an approved tool. But even if these decisions are unintentional, they can cause huge risks to organizations. In this article, we'll look at why shadow IT happens, and why it's become such a big problem lately. We’ll provide a practical, three-step approach to fixing it for good, and explore where the right Data Loss Prevention (DLP) tool fits in. What is shadow IT, and why is it such a liability? Shadow IT is any technology, including apps, software, devices, AI tools, and cloud services, that employees use for work without the knowledge or approval of the IT department . And lately, shadow IT has been booming: Gartner predicts 75% of employees will be acquiring or modifying technology outside official IT visibility by 2027. When IT is unaware of the shadow IT being used, it can’t monitor what information is being shared, or what privileges are being granted to apps and tools. This makes the use of Shadow IT particularly susceptible to exploitation by hackers. In most cases, shadow IT isn’t used maliciously – people are simply looking for ways to do their jobs better and faster. But often these decisions prioritize speed over safety, creating unintended risks that can threaten the whole organization. Consider this scenario: you need to share a 400MB video file with a client, but your company's approved file-sharing cap is at 25MB. The client is making a decision tomorrow, and IT takes at least two weeks to reply, making it easier to just use WeTransfer instead of waiting on an official approval. Just like that, shadow IT has crept into your workflow . Shadow IT doesn't only come from employees ignoring policy. It comes from policies and systems that are too rigid, too slow, or too out of step with how people actually work. And these shortcomings are causing serious harm: studies show around 11% of all cyber incidents happen thanks to shadow IT. Speaking of how people actually work, have you read our practical cybersecurity checklist yet? Get it for free right here . 15 Key Cybersecurity Practices for Every Employee Real-life Shadow IT stories: what went wrong Before we get into why shadow IT is booming, let’s take a look at a few familiar shadow IT examples – and the real-world incidents that caused such a big headache for companies. The Personal Laptop Scenario: A member of your team needs to work remotely for a few days, but they’ve left their work computer in the office, so they use their personal laptop. IRL example: Nikkei leaked sensitive data for 17,000 customers in 2025 after an employee logged in to Slack from their personal computer, which was infected with malware. The WhatsApp War Room Scenario: An operations team decides coordinating over personal phones is much easier because the official comms tool requires three separate approvals just to add a contact, and they can’t be bothered. IRL example: Over a dozen major banks were fined over $2 billion in 2022, in part because employees conducted business on WhatsApp and other unauthorized messaging platforms that firms and regulators couldn't keep tabs on. The Rogue Trello Board Scenario: A project is managed on a free-tier Trello account because the enterprise project management tool takes weeks to grant access, and budgets are tight. IRL example: In 2016, a UN board leaked credentials for an internal file server through misconfigured, publicly visible Trello boards that nobody in security was tracking. The Shadow AI Stack Scenario: Several employees are running sensitive data through public versions of ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini because there's no approved internal AI tool in place. IRL example: Samsung famously banned ChatGPT in 2023 after employees pasted sensitive source code into an open version of the tool, adding this code to its training dataset. The Smartwatch Loophole Scenario: A government agency has a strict policy on using official devices with WiFi or bluetooth capabilities in secure office environments in which highly sensitive material is handled, but allows employees to wear unsecured smartwatches. IRL example: In 2025, researchers demonstrated the possibility of stealing data in secure air-gapped environments via hacking smartwatches. Each of these examples follows the same pattern: a genuine business need is met by the fastest available tool, with no security team in the loop, and this creates the risk of unintentional data breaches, exfiltration, and other attacks. Let’s dig deeper on why more people have been using unauthorized tools lately. Why shadow IT is exploding (hint: it's not just remote work) The growth of shadow IT over the last decade comes down to a few consistent factors: The approval process is broken. Employees often wait weeks for IT to approve tools that take thirty seconds to sign up for themselves. There’s a gap in awareness. People may not understand that there are rules in place around which devices, software, or apps should be used for work. Similarly, they may not realize how these tools can be used against them – and their workplace. Consumer tech has lapped enterprise tech on user experience. The free version of a tool is often far better designed, and easier to use, than whatever IT provides. Business moves faster than official processes. If a busy lead insists on chatting over WhatsApp to get things moving when a day’s delay could cost the opportunity, of course a sales rep is going to take a call on the unsecured platform. The AI wildcard. Shadow AI is accelerating everything, with ChatGPT, Copilot plugins, and browser extensions used across departments IT has never heard of, and often with sensitive data flowing straight into them. Read more: Smishing Explained: The Threat Vector CISOs Can No Longer Ignore Shadow IT risks: why this is more than an IT housekeeping issue So what are the shadow IT risks, in practical terms? Security exposure: Unsanctioned tools don’t go through security vetting. There's no enforced MFA, no patch management, and no visibility for the security team, which can expose organizations to the threat of data breaches, malware, and more. Compliance landmines: Regulations like GDPR, HIPAA, and PCI-DSS are routinely violated by shadow IT tools that mishandle data residency or handling requirements, often without anyone realizing it until it's too late. The invisible attack surface: You can't protect what you can't see. Security teams working from an incomplete asset inventory are, in effect, flying blind – especially when it comes to unsanctioned file sharing via tools that aren’t even on the IT radar. Data silos and lost institutional knowledge: When the employee who built that rogue Airtable base leaves the company, the data and the knowledge of how it was structured leaves with them. New channels for social engineering: If employees are using a platform, chances are cyber attackers are using it too. And because there’s no visibility for security teams, social engineering is more likely to succeed. Unfortunately, these risks are more widespread than you might realize: according to Netskope, an astonishing 97% of cloud apps used within enterprise-level companies are not managed by a centralized IT or security team. That figure alone should reframe how most leadership teams think about their actual exposure. Shadow AI — the biggest threat of all? Shadow AI, when employees use public versions of generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and AI browser plugins without IT or security approval, is arguably the fastest-evolving and least understood category of shadow IT risk. The risk here is serious. The output of these tools can contain company IP and sensitive data that end up feeding training models or sitting on third-party servers indefinitely. Here’s a common pattern: a developer pastes proprietary source code into an AI assistant to help debug it. That code is now potentially stored in a third-party system and could be reproduced in part elsewhere. Simply banning AI tools doesn't work, as this only pushes usage further underground, where it's harder to detect and govern. The real opportunity lies with organizations that get ahead of this by using approved AI tooling: they get the productivity upside and the security controls, rather than choosing between the two. Read more: Cyber Month Spotlight: 5 AI Threats and How to Beat Them See it, simplify it, solve it: 3 key steps to actually fixing shadow IT for good Shadow IT can feel like an unsolvable problem, but it isn't. Here's our practical, three-step approach to defining shadow IT and fixing it for good. Step 1: See it — get some visibility You can't fix what you can't see, so the first job is shadow IT detection : mapping out the actual scale and scope of the problem inside your organization. Deploy a Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) to discover what's genuinely running across your network. Audit OAuth permissions. Most security teams are genuinely shocked by what employees have authorized over time, including overscoped permissions, or access grants from long-abandoned pilot tools. Check expense reports. Employees expensing SaaS subscriptions is one of the clearest signs of shadow IT available, and it's often sitting in plain sight in your finance system already. Use a good Data Loss Prevention (DLP) tool to track and map file-sharing practices, including those that could extend beyond your official data use policy. Step 2: Simplify it — fix the process and the policy Once you understand the scale of the problem, the next step is shadow IT management: addressing the process gaps that created the need for unapproved tools in the first place. Create a "fast track" approval lane for low-risk tools, with a target turnaround of 48 hours rather than weeks. Run a "shadow IT amnesty." Invite employees to come forward about what they're actually using, without penalty or negative repercussions. Talk to employees directly about why they're using these tools. This almost always points to a gap in your approved stack or a friction point in your approval process. Revisit your Acceptable Use policy and assess where it still holds up, where it might need adjusting, and how you can make sure your teams understand it. Step 3: Solve it — build a culture where IT is a partner, not a gatekeeper Now, this is where the long-term shadow IT policy work really pays off: building a collaborative culture where IT doesn’t get in the way, but actually enables people. First, find the right security awareness training to help frame shadow IT as a shared risk rather than purely a rules violation. Give people approved alternatives that are actually good. If your file-sharing tool still caps uploads at 25MB in 2026, that's on IT to fix, not on employees to work around. Select an approved AI environment with a secure private version – before employees build one for themselves. Combine all of this with an Employee Security Posture Management tool that helps you proactively track risky behaviors around device permissions and data sharing. And remember, your goal isn't zero shadow IT; that's not realistic. The goal is zero unknown shadow IT – and with these steps, you can get there. None of this works, though, if you can’t see the data leaving in the first place – and that’s where DLP comes in. Choose a DLP tool that sees the shadow IT risk before it happens A good DLP tool flags sensitive data heading to unsanctioned apps (personal email, unauthorized cloud storage, unsanctioned destinations), turning shadow IT from an invisible problem into one you can act on. With SaaS sprawl accelerating across every department, cloud DLP isn’t a nice-to-have; it’s a baseline shadow IT control. But DLP catches the symptom, not the cause, and it only works on data it can see. Some DLP tools can struggle with unmanaged devices, encrypted traffic, and shadow SaaS/shadow AI tools where data is typed into a prompt, rather than sent as a file. That's why your choice of DLP tool is so important. You need SaaS DLP that covers the platforms your organization actually relies on, including DLP for Google Drive and DLP for Microsoft, since that's where most collaboration and most accidental data transfer happen. At Riot, we understand these needs, because we’ve been there ourselves. That’s why we built Sonar : to help teams manage how they share data with partners and across cloud platforms, and to catch exposure before it becomes an incident. Now, before we finish up, let’s look quickly at what you should include in your acceptable use policy. Shadow IT essentials: what should you include in your acceptable use policy? A strong shadow IT, acceptable use, or information security policy should cover: A clear definition of what requires approval, and what doesn't. A fast-track request process. A clear split between employee and IT responsibilities. Consequences for non-compliance, but include amnesty provisions. Specific guidance on AI tools and personal devices. Guidance for regular security reviews – ideally quarterly, not annually. Get your internal policy right, and you can give your teams the clarity they need to understand the true risks of shadow IT and unapproved devices. The real key to solving shadow IT? Be a coach, not a cop One last reminder to finish up: The strictest IT department has the most shadow IT. This isn’t to say we shouldn’t try to monitor shadow IT at all. But instead of policing our teams, we need to coach them to do better. Shadow IT will never disappear entirely, and honestly, you shouldn't want that. Employees resourceful enough to find their own solutions to real problems are employees worth keeping – but they need some guardrails. The organizations that make shadow IT a lot less scary are the ones that make the approved path so fast and so easy that going rogue simply isn't necessary anymore. But to do this, you need to drive awareness of the risks and invest in a good set of tools for the job. To boost your team's awareness of shadow IT risks and limit your exposure with our DLP solution Sonar, chat to one of our experts today. FAQ What is shadow IT? Shadow IT is any technology (apps, software, devices, AI tools, or cloud services) that employees use for work without the knowledge or approval of the IT department. Why is shadow IT so risky? It creates security exposure, compliance gaps, and an attack surface that security teams can't see or manage, since unsanctioned tools bypass standard vetting and controls. How can attackers use shadow IT against us? Attackers target the same unofficial channels and apps employees are already using, knowing these tools sit outside the visibility of security teams. How do we manage the risks involved with shadow IT? Start with visibility (discovery and auditing), simplify your approval process and policy, and build a culture where IT processes aren’t a barrier. What about shadow AI? Shadow AI is currently the fastest-growing and riskiest category of shadow IT, since sensitive data and IP can be typed directly into prompts with no oversight. How can DLP help? A Data Loss Prevention (DLP) tool gives you visibility into where sensitive data is moving, helping you turn shadow IT from an invisible problem into one you can actually act on. title: The Misleading World of “Healthy” Advice
summary: Uncover the truth behind common “healthy” advice. Learn how trends, myths, and misinformation can lead you away from real wellbeing and evidence-based habits.
body_text: In this episode of The Orange Club Podcast , Dietician Nidhi Nigam talks about a silent yet powerful force shaping the health choices of today’s generation, misinformation. From misleading food labels to unqualified influencers, half-baked advice is everywhere, and it’s affecting how people eat, think, and live. Watch the clip here: Debunking “Healthy” Advice The Power of Popularity Over Expertise A large following doesn’t equal authority. Many social media influencers share “tips” that sound convincing but lack scientific grounding. As Nidhi explains, “People who don’t have the knowledge or authority are still dictating terms because they have 100K or 200K followers and people are listening to them.” This blind trust is creating confusion and unhealthy habits among those genuinely trying to make better choices. Food Labels That Tell Only Half the Story Marketing language on food products often paints a misleading picture. Words like “natural,” “sugar-free,” or “low-fat” can be deceiving; they don’t always mean the product is healthy. For many consumers, this “health halo” effect leads to choices that look good on the shelf but aren’t truly good for the body. Why It’s Time to Question the Source Before taking any advice about what to eat or buy, it’s important to ask a simple question: Who is giving me this information? As Nidhi points out, the credibility of the person matters as much as the content itself. Checking for professional qualifications, such as certified nutritionists or medical professionals can help filter out noise from genuine guidance. Informed Choices Begin With Awareness Health isn’t about trends, it’s about trust. By staying aware and learning to question the “why” behind every claim, we can protect ourselves from misleading advice and make decisions rooted in knowledge, not hype. Watch the full conversation on The Orange Club Podcast - All About Nutrition , where Dietician Nidhi Nigam shares more insights on navigating the chaos of modern health information and choosing what truly works for you.

title: Why Financial Advisors Should Target Young Investors
body_text: As this generation grows older, its purchasing power will increase, which means millennials will want to move their money. Advisors need to show them that the opportunities they offer align with millennials’ style. They are already earning more than past young adults did at their age. However, since millennials came of age during that 2008 recession, they are leery about investing. This is a generation of skeptical, analytical, and tech-reliant people who are also full of potential. They need to put their money with trustworthy, relatable advisors who are as adaptable as they are. Because financial enterprises are consistently seeking the next big growth opportunity, they may want to turn their attention to this lucrative investor base for three major reasons: The Great Wealth Transfer Baby boomers will soon transfer their wealth to their children, making now an opportune time for advisors to capture new clientele. According to CNBC , no less than $68 trillion is about to change hands in the U.S., making it the “biggest wealth transfer in history.” Where do financial advisors come into play? Studies show that 66 percent of children switch advisors after they receive their inheritance, so you’ll want to make sure that you’re accessible, attentive, and committed to everything young investors need in an advisor to ensure your business is right there when these transfers happen. Long-Run Potential When managing a business, it’s crucial that you keep both your short-term and long-term revenue in mind. While it’s true that young investors are just beginning their careers and have fewer assets, it’s also true that as they continue their careers, their assets will grow. By snagging them early and building a relationship, you’ll be top of mind as those assets increase. Part of this long-term potential lies in the fact that young investors need guidance on how to reduce financial stress. Advisors would do well to provide financial literacy for young clients, because there’s currently a significant market for it. Targeting Young Investors Will Keep You Competitive Younger investors prefer a fiduciary approach regarding investments. Adding new skills and benefits to your practice is going to make you more competitive in the marketplace. Only 4.5 percent of the U.S. population has $1 million or more in investable assets; financial professionals who only help the wealthy population will miss a big opportunity to help young investors who have fewer financial resources. Most of the population is middle or working class, which opens the door for advisors to bridge this wealth gap. If you make it the mission of your business to help young investors - who aren’t already rich - achieve financial security, they’ll likely stick with your business for the long haul. The old ways of financial advising are dead and gone. As wealth transfers from baby boomers to millennials, advisors must learn to adapt. Until now, the industry hasn’t functioned to serve the needs of the average investor who is living paycheck to paycheck – however, that’s exactly what young investors today need. From total transparency to compelling visuals, there are several key ways to engage with younger investors: Comprehensive Financial Services In order to provide truly comprehensive financial services, you have to offer more than just financial advice – you also have to offer financial guidance. One of the biggest challenges young investors face is a lack of financial knowledge – when it comes to their finances, they’ve been “winging it.” Financial advisors can remedy this gap in education by providing more than just advice. When a major life event comes up, such as marriage, advisors should help younger clients with concerns such as: Combining and balancing finances Saving for down payments on major purchases like autos and homes Securing the right types and amount of insurance coverages Determining whether to pay off certain debts before applying for major loans In addition, many millennials are launching their careers with significant student debt and need financial advisors who are able to help them manage it. Advisors who aren’t well-versed on the subject must educate themselves in order to attract young investors who need help with such a complex topic. Advisors should be able to help them navigate requirements and paperwork, create budgets and manage spending, and ultimately pay off debt. Communication with Convenience Young investors have different tastes from their older counterparts: They prefer robo-advisors, remote communication, email, text messaging, and social media. In fact, almost 90 percent of millennials claim that they are never without their mobile phones . This means you’ll need to ensure that your young investors can communicate and access information via these mobile devices. Information must be made easily available across a variety of platforms. Likewise, millennials won’t always be able to meet with their financial advisors in person, either. Make meetings available and accessible via video or phone so they can connect from anywhere in the world. An added benefit of sharpening your skills to adjust for a younger audience is that you’ll attract and retain older audiences as well. For example, if you add that video conferencing capability to your suite of services to appeal to a younger audience, older investors may also find the convenience of conferences useful. Transparency Goes the Distance Members of the younger investing generation are skeptical truth seekers. This means you’ll need to provide each investor with all the pertinent information with respect to potential business opportunities. Be upfront right at the start about disclosing fees. Traditionally, financial planners didn’t disclose fees until clients met with them. However, younger investors don’t want to waste time traveling to the office if the partnership will not be affordable. Plainly display your fee and costs on your website. Be sure to include concise information about how fees will be calculated. For example, potential clients will want to know upfront if fees are based on a percentage of assets under management or income. Inclusivity and Diversity Matters Younger investors are decidedly inclusive and diverse, so you’ll want to attract these potential clients by ensuring that your business is on the same page. There are many areas in the United States in which English is not a main tongue – in fact, it is estimated that there are over 350 different languages spoken in the United States. In Los Angeles, for example, over half of the city’s population speaks English in the office or at school but rarely – or not at all – once they return home. Embrace inclusivity and diversity, by providing multi-lingual customer service and adding diversity to your team. Advisors can also focus on languages in addition to English in their mobile apps for wider brand reach. Mobile devices are personal - they provide a virtual space where consumers revert to their true selves and, consequently, to their mother tongues. If you keep your app monolingual, you’ll miss major business opportunities with young investors. Translation opens up new markets and expands the reach of your mobile app. The Cause Effect Millennials, more than any other generation, are looking for ways to put their money to work for social and environmental change. They make up a group of investors who are inching toward their peak earning years. 21.7 percent of millennials say that the single most important factor when making investments is the goals of the companies in which they are investing. Over 60 percent of millennials surveyed in early 2019 by TD Ameritrade had at least 21 percent of their money in ESG investments. These investments that promote environmental, social, or governance goals speak volumes about the generational mindset of young investors. They want their money to make an impact in the world. A study by the wealth management division of Bank of America also found that 37 percent of high net worth investors reviewed their investment portfolios for ESG impact , and the biggest one-year increase (+14%) was from millennials. Be sure that your company communicates the ESG priority to young investors — let them know that your business recognizes its importance and values their commitment to it. Obstacle Removal Three main obstacles currently stand in the way of getting more millennials to explore investment opportunities: speed, complexity, and cost. These young investors don’t want to wait for transactions to be processed; they’ve been raised in the age of “nowism”. They are used to instant answers and don’t want to deal with layers of red tape and legal fine print. Young investors are very risk-averse, in large part due to the effects of the recession of 2008. They appreciate trial investment methods that come with an affordable cost of entry, especially when they are new to investing. Your business will need to focus on lifting the barriers of cost, complexity, and speed in order to attract millennial investors – which would likely appeal to Gen Xers and baby boomer investors, as well. Understand the Millennial Lifestyle Make it a priority to become familiar with your clients’ values and missions so that you can properly guide these up-and-coming young conscientious investors. Be sure to keep the list of “can’t-dos” to a minimum. No one, especially those in the younger working generation, wants to repeatedly be told that they must be a miser with their money and not spend any of it. Focus on finding a prudent balance. When your business creates budgets for young investors, include money for vacations and outings. While it’s true that they want to invest and also save for retirement, they don’t want to do so at the expense of living their lives now. The volatility of the markets and the Great Recession of 2008 have resulted in a state of general skepticism toward financial institutions among young potential investors. In addition, this clientele demands requirements of wealth managers that are different from previous generations. Millennials will soon be the largest group of potential investment clients, driving many financial advisors to reassess their business models. Early adoption is going to enable financial professionals to successfully serve young investors and, in turn, keep their leading position and protect their market share. title: Flowly Launches "Pathways to Healing" Fund to Support Access to Chronic Pain Recovery Program
body_text: Flowly Launches "Pathways to Healing" Fund to Support Access to Chronic Pain Recovery Program Los Angeles, CA, November 20, 2024 — Flowly, the innovate startup backed by the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and Y Combinator (YC), is proud to announce the launch of the "Pathways to Healing" fund, a new initiative aimed at making the Healing from Pain program more accessible to those who need it most. The fund will officially launch on Giving Tuesday , a global day of generosity, on December 3, 2024 . The Pathways to Healing fund was established to address the financial barriers that many individuals face when seeking effective, non-pharmaceutical treatments for chronic pain. While Flowly currently accepts certain health insurance plans in select states, the need for accessible pain management solutions has far exceeded coverage limitations. This initiative aligns with Flowly’s core mission of democratizing access to effective pain management solutions, by providing financial support for those who are unable to afford the full cost of the program. Healing from Pain is an evidence-backed, at-home program designed to help individuals manage chronic pain and stress. Developed in collaboration with leading pain therapists and supported by the NIH, Flowly’s unique approach leverages personalized virtual pain therapy sessions, immersive VR experiences, and Heart Rate Variability (HRV) training to help users build resilience and reduce pain perception over time. "We believe everyone deserves a chance to live a life free from pain," said Celine Tien, CEO and Founder. "At Flowly, we’ve seen a surge in demand for our program as people look for ways to manage their chronic pain. While we are covered by several health plans, we recognize that many individuals remain without coverage or don’t have the financial means to pay for Flowly out-of-pocket. The Pathways to Healing fund is our way of ensuring that financial barriers don’t stand in the way of someone accessing the care they need.” How It Works The Pathways to Healing fund will offer financial assistance to individuals who apply for the Healing from Pain program and meet specific eligibility criteria. The goal is to provide partial or full financial support, ensuring that cost is not a barrier to accessing this life-changing program. About Flowly and the Healing from Pain program Flowly is a virtual clinic designed for the 1 in 5 Americans living with chronic pain. Flowly’s 12-week Healing from Pain program is focused on nonstructural pain, empowering patients to manage pain, anxiety, and stress in their day-to-day lives. Flowly integrates behavioral health support through licensed therapists trained in pain psychology, along with a proprietary at-home VR and biofeedback system that enables self-guided practice. Providers can partner with Flowly to offer their patients on-demand access to the latest in pain psychology and therapeutic techniques, easing the burden on clinics by supporting patients’ mental and emotional health from home. To learn more about Flowly, please visit flowly.world.

body_text: GLP-1 medications can lower appetite, make meals smaller, and support meaningful weight progress. Those changes can be meaningful, especially when they support health goals you have been working toward. But your hair can respond to those changes too. When food intake drops quickly, the body may get less protein, fewer calories, and fewer hair-supporting nutrients than it needs. That can push more hairs into the resting phase and lead to temporary shedding, often called telogen effluvium. This kind of shedding can feel sudden and discouraging, especially when your medication is helping in other areas of your health. In many cases, the follicles are resting while the body adjusts. A steadier routine can help you support the next growth cycle with less panic and less guesswork. Start with four practical steps: eat, test, care, and wait. 01 Eat Prioritize protein before fullness sets in. 02 Test Check for nutrient gaps before starting multiple supplements. 03 Care Keep the scalp and strands gentle while the cycle recovers. 04 Wait Give the hair cycle time to reset. Why Hair Shedding Can Happen During a GLP-1 Routine GLP-1 medications can affect appetite, fullness, digestion, and daily eating habits. As meals get smaller or easier to skip, nutrition can become harder to maintain consistently. Hair growth depends on energy, protein, micronutrients, hormones, and a stable internal environment. During rapid weight change or lower intake, the body may give less energy to hair growth for a while. We use "nutrient gap" as a simple way to describe what can happen when lower appetite, smaller portions, nausea, food aversions, or rapid weight change makes steady nutrition harder to maintain. It is not a diagnosis, and it does not mean everyone taking a GLP-1 medication has low nutrient levels. Hair shedding may become more noticeable when several changes happen at once: Possible Change During a GLP-1 Routine Why It May Affect Hair Lower appetite Smaller meals may make it harder to get enough protein and hair-supporting nutrients. Skipped meals Fewer meals can mean fewer chances to support hair-building nutrition. Rapid weight change Fast body change can act as a stress signal to the hair cycle. Lower protein intake Hair depends on amino acids to support the next growth cycle. Nutrient gaps Iron, zinc, vitamin D, B12, biotin, and healthy fats may all play a role in hair and scalp wellness. Overlapping triggers Stress, illness, thyroid changes, postpartum changes, menopause, or existing thinning can make shedding more visible. GLP-1-related shedding needs a full-body view. The medication may be one part of the picture because it can change appetite and weight, while the hair cycle may be responding to lower intake, faster body change, or overlapping health factors. What Medication Labels Can Tell Us About Hair Shedding Some GLP-1 and related weight-management medication labels include hair loss reports. For example, Wegovy's prescribing information notes that hair-loss adverse reactions in Wegovy-treated patients were associated with weight reduction. In pooled adult studies, hair loss was reported in 3.3% of patients treated with Wegovy 2.4 mg compared with 1% of patients treated with placebo. The label also notes that hair loss was reported in 4% of pediatric patients treated with Wegovy 2.4 mg and in no placebo-treated pediatric patients. In other words, the label points to weight change as part of the picture. It does not show that the medication directly damages the hair follicle. A balanced support plan should look at food intake, possible labs, scalp care, medication guidance, and recovery time. Eat: Prioritize Protein Before Fullness Sets In Step 01 — Eat When appetite is lower, protein can drop without much warning. You may still be eating, but smaller portions can make it harder to get enough protein across the day. Hair is largely made from keratin, a structural protein. Your body needs amino acids to support the next growth cycle, so protein is one of the first places to check when shedding begins during a GLP-1 routine. A protein-first approach can help. Choose protein earlier in the meal, before you feel too full to continue eating. This does not require large meals or an extreme diet. It helps smaller meals do more for your body. Helpful protein-first habits may include: Add protein to breakfast before coffee, errands, or a busy workday. Choose smaller protein-rich meals if large meals feel uncomfortable. Keep easy protein options available for low-appetite days. Avoid letting nausea or fullness lead to repeated under-eating. Ask a clinician or dietitian about a realistic daily protein target. Helpful protein options may include eggs, Greek yogurt, fish, poultry, tofu, lentils, beans, cottage cheese, protein smoothies, and nut butters. Protein is a strong first check-in, and it works alongside other nutrients. If shedding feels heavy, lasts longer than expected, or comes with other symptoms, lab testing may help you understand what your body needs next. Test: Check for Nutrient Gaps Before Starting Multiple Supplements Step 02 — Test Hair shedding can make supplements feel urgent. Adding several at once can create more confusion, especially when you do not know whether your body needs them. Iron, vitamin D, B12, zinc, biotin, and healthy fats can all support hair and scalp wellness. High-dose supplements are not right for everyone, and biotin can interfere with some lab results. Tell your clinician if you take biotin or are considering it before bloodwork. If shedding feels heavy, prolonged, or paired with other symptoms, ask your healthcare provider whether lab work makes sense. Possible labs to discuss may include: Ferritin or iron status Vitamin D Vitamin B12 Thyroid markers Zinc, when appropriate Other labs based on your symptoms, diet, medications, and medical history This is especially helpful if shedding comes with fatigue, dizziness, weakness, brittle nails, heavy periods, menstrual changes, cold intolerance, restrictive eating, or unexplained illness. Hair Need GLP-1-Related Challenge Support Step Protein Smaller meals may reduce protein intake. Eat protein earlier in the meal. Iron Lower intake may worsen low stores. Ask about ferritin or iron labs. Zinc Restrictive eating may reduce intake. Discuss with a clinician. Vitamin D Low levels are common for many people. Ask if testing makes sense. B12 Diet variety may drop. Ask about B12 testing. Biotin and B vitamins Diet changes may affect intake for some people. Discuss supplements with a clinician, especially before labs. Healthy fats Very low-calorie eating may reduce fats. Include balanced meals when possible. Once you have a better sense of the internal support your body may need, the next step is caring for the hair and scalp you are managing day to day. Care: Keep the Scalp and Strands Gentle Step 03 — Care GLP-1-related shedding often begins with changes inside the body, but your daily routine can affect how your hair feels while the cycle recovers. When hair feels thinner or more fragile, harsh handling can add breakage. Shedding and breakage are different, but both can make hair look and feel thinner. You can keep washing, conditioning, and caring for your hair. Focus on reducing unnecessary stress on the scalp and strands while your body stabilizes. Gentle hair and scalp habits may include: Cleanse the scalp without harsh scrubbing. Use conditioner to reduce friction and improve manageability. Detangle slowly, especially when hair is wet or fragile. Avoid tight hairstyles during heavy shedding. Limit high heat, bleaching, and aggressive brushing. Keep your routine consistent instead of changing several products at once. The hairs that shed during telogen effluvium were often already ready to release. Gentle washing usually reveals those hairs; it is usually not the cause of the shedding. How Reviv3 Fits Into a GLP-1 Hair Support Routine Reviv3 helps support a consistent scalp and hair care routine while your body adjusts to appetite, weight, and nutrition changes. PREP PREP Cleanser Shampoo helps cleanse the scalp and remove buildup so the scalp feels fresh and ready for the rest of your routine. Shop PREP → PRIME PRIME Moisture+ Conditioner helps soften and condition the hair fiber, which can make dry or fragile strands feel more manageable during shedding. Shop PRIME → TREAT TREAT Micro-Active3 Treatment works as a leave-in scalp-care step for targeted support. Shop TREAT → BOOST BOOST Biotin Cellular Complex provides topical scalp-focused support for areas where thinning looks more noticeable. Shop BOOST → Reviv3 works alongside nutrition support, medical guidance, and your prescriber's advice. It helps you care for the scalp and strands with calm, repeatable steps while the hair cycle recovers. Wait: Give the Hair Cycle Time to Reset Step 04 — Wait Hair recovery takes time because the hair cycle moves slowly. With telogen effluvium, shedding often appears a few months after the trigger. Research notes that acute telogen effluvium often happens two to three months after a stressor or body change and usually lasts three to six months. Hair loss may show up after appetite changes, weight loss, nausea, stress, or nutrition changes have already been happening for a while. Recovery can also lag behind the support you are adding now. Even after nutrition becomes more consistent and shedding begins to slow, visible fullness may take several months to improve. Try to watch for gradual signs of stabilization: Fewer strands in the shower or brush Less shedding during wash day A steadier ponytail or part line over time Short new hairs near the hairline or part Less breakage from styling and detangling Do not stop taking a prescribed GLP-1 medication without speaking to your prescriber. Hair shedding is often temporary and supportable, while your medication may be helping with important health needs. Your clinician can help you weigh benefits, side effects, dosage, nutrition, and next steps. How to Manage GLP-1 Hair Shedding Without Overcorrecting When hair starts shedding, it is natural to want to fix everything right away. You may feel tempted to cut calories further, stop washing your hair, try several new supplements, switch products every few days, or question whether you should stop your medication altogether. Your body, scalp, and strands usually need steadier support. If your appetite is already lower, cutting calories further can make the nutrient gap harder on your hair. If fullness, nausea, or food aversion makes eating difficult, talk to your prescriber about support instead of trying to push through it alone. Your hair also needs gentler handling during this season. Tight hairstyles, aggressive brushing, bleaching, high heat, and frequent product changes can add extra stress when strands already feel fragile. A better next step is to simplify. Prioritize protein, ask about labs if symptoms suggest a possible gap, keep scalp care gentle and consistent, avoid harsh styling habits, track shedding for a few weeks, and talk to your clinician if shedding feels severe, sudden, or persistent. GLP-1 Hair Shedding in Women: When Hormones, Iron, and Weight Loss Overlap For many women, hair shedding shows up in the places they see and feel every day: a wider part, thinner temples, a smaller ponytail, or more hair in their hands after wash day. That can feel especially frustrating when a GLP-1 medication is helping your body change in a positive direction. You may feel proud of your progress and still feel unsettled by what is happening to your hair. Women may also have overlapping triggers to consider. GLP-1-related weight loss can happen at the same time as postpartum changes, perimenopause, menopause, heavy periods, thyroid changes, stress, or low iron stores. A next step plan can include eating protein consistently, asking your clinician about ferritin, thyroid, vitamin D, B12, and zinc testing, avoiding tight ponytails or harsh brushing, using a gentle scalp-first routine, giving regrowth time, and seeing a dermatologist if shedding lasts longer than expected or density keeps declining. When to Talk to a Doctor About GLP-1 Hair Shedding GLP-1-related shedding is often temporary, but you do not have to guess your way through it. A doctor or dermatologist can help confirm whether the shedding fits telogen effluvium or whether another factor may be involved, such as nutrient deficiency, thyroid changes, genetic thinning, scalp irritation, or a medical condition. Talk to a healthcare provider or dermatologist if hair loss is: Patchy, painful, scaly, red, or inflamed Associated with sores, itching, or burning Happening with sudden bald spots Lasting longer than six months Getting worse over time You should also ask for medical guidance if shedding comes with fatigue, dizziness, weakness, heavy periods, menstrual changes, thyroid symptoms, restrictive eating, or unexplained illness. Common Questions About GLP-1 Hair Shedding Can GLP-1 medications cause hair loss? Some people report hair shedding while using GLP-1 medications, especially when treatment is paired with rapid weight change, lower appetite, or changes in daily nutrition. For many people, the most likely type of shedding is telogen effluvium, a temporary response that can happen after physical stress or major body change. Is hair loss a side effect of GLP-1 medications? Hair shedding may happen during a GLP-1 routine, but it is often difficult to separate the medication from the body changes that may happen during treatment. Appetite changes, weight loss, nutrient intake, stress, hormones, and existing hair concerns can all influence the hair cycle. What should I do first if my hair starts shedding on a GLP-1 medication? Start with protein, meal consistency, gentle scalp care, and medical guidance when needed. Ask about lab testing if shedding feels heavy or comes with fatigue, weakness, menstrual changes, restrictive eating, or other symptoms. What are the best nutrients for GLP-1 hair shedding? Protein, iron, zinc, vitamin D, B12, biotin, and healthy fats may all support hair and scalp wellness. The best plan depends on your diet, symptoms, lab results, medications, and health needs. Ask a clinician before starting high-dose supplements, especially because biotin can interfere with some lab results. How long does GLP-1 hair shedding last? If the shedding is telogen effluvium, it may last several months. Many people begin to notice improvement once weight loss slows, nutrition becomes more consistent, and the hair cycle has time to recover. Visible fullness may take longer because regrowth is gradual. Should I stop my GLP-1 medication if my hair is falling out? Do not stop taking a prescribed medication without speaking to your prescriber. Hair shedding is often temporary, while your medication may be supporting important health needs. Your clinician can help you weigh benefits, side effects, dosage, nutrition, and next steps. GLP-1 Hair Shedding Support Starts With Steady Steps GLP-1 medications can support meaningful health progress, but quick changes in appetite, weight, and nutrition can ask more from your body than expected. When that happens, your hair cycle may pause, shed, and slowly reset. Shedding can feel discouraging, but it can also be a sign to support your body more steadily while it adjusts. Start with the four-step plan: eat, test, care, and wait. Prioritize protein before fullness sets in. Ask about clinician-guided labs if symptoms suggest a possible nutrient gap. Care for your scalp and strands gently. Give the hair cycle time to recover. Reviv3 fits into that plan as the scalp-first support step. A steady routine can help you care for the scalp and strands while nutrition, medical guidance, and time support the internal side of recovery. For a more complete hair-support routine, many customers combine the Reviv3 haircare regimen with hair growth gummies like FOLLY, a supplement brand positioned for concerns including GLP-1 shedding, postpartum changes, and hormonal changes. Together, the routine supports scalp and strand care from the outside while adding nutrition-focused support from within. Support your scalp while your body adjusts. title: TScan Therapeutics Announces First Patient Dosed in Phase 3 ALLOHA-2™, a Pivotal Trial Evaluating TSC-101 in Patients with Heme Malignancies
summary: Actively enrolling patients across the US with anticipated topline data readout mid-2028 WALTHAM, Mass., July 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- TScan Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: TCRX), a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on the development of T cell receptor (TCR)-engineered T cell (TCR-T)
body_text: Actively enrolling patients across the US with anticipated topline data readout mid-2028 WALTHAM, Mass., July 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- TScan Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: TCRX), a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on the development of T cell receptor (TCR)-engineered T cell (TCR-T) therapies for the treatment of patients with cancer, today announced that the first patient has been infused with TSC-101 in the pivotal Phase 3 ALLOHA-2™ trial (NCT07702578). The patient, who was enrolled in June, has now received their first infusion of TSC-101 following successful stem cell engraftment. The trial is investigating the efficacy and safety of TSC-101 for the treatment of residual disease to prevent relapse following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS). “Dosing our first patient in the ALLOHA-2™ study is a significant milestone for TScan. Having been a part of TScan as we moved TSC-101 from an idea to Discovery, through Phase 1 clinical development, and now to a Phase 3 study, I want to acknowledge all the hard work that went into bringing TSC-101 to this integral step and congratulate all current and previous members of the TScan team,” said Gavin MacBeath, Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer. “I would also like to thank the investigators, the patients, and their families for participating in our Phase 1 ALLOHA™ trial. In June, we reported initial data from Cohort C of that study, in which patients were treated with our commercial-ready manufacturing process. The strong clinical efficacy and positive safety profile observed in this cohort gives us added confidence in our Phase 3 trial and future clinical development plans.” “TSC-101 has demonstrated a safety profile and clinical results that continue to excite the transplant community,” said Chrystal U. Louis, M.D., Chief Medical Officer. “The pace of Cohort C enrollment highlights the growing interest in TSC-101 as a potential therapeutic option for people with AML or MDS, and we look forward to working with our investigators to address residual disease and improve survival in patients after allo-HCT.” The Phase 3 ALLOHA-2™ pivotal trial is a study evaluating TSC-101 administered after standard of care HCT vs HCT alone in patients with AML or MDS. Treatment is based on biological assignment (genetic randomization), with A*02:01-positive subjects with an appropriate donor assigned to the treatment arm, and A*02:01-negative subjects, or A*02:01-posititve subjects without an appropriate donor, assigned to the control arm. All subjects will receive HCT with reduced intensity conditioning. Subjects in the treatment arm will receive two infusions of TSC-101 following engraftment. The primary endpoint for the study is relapse-free survival, and key secondary endpoints include overall survival and event-free survival. To learn more about the ALLOHA-2™ clinical trial, visit clinicaltrials.gov (identifier: NCT07702578). About TScan Therapeutics, Inc. TScan is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on the development of T cell receptor (TCR)-engineered T cell (TCR-T) therapies for the treatment of patients with cancer. The Company’s lead TCR-T therapy candidate, TSC-101, is in development for the treatment of patients with hematologic malignancies to prevent relapse following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (the ALLOHA-2™ Phase 3 pivotal trial). The Company is also in early stages of developing methods for in vivo engineering to treat solid tumors. In addition, the Company is applying its target discovery platform to discover novel targets in various T cell-mediated autoimmune disorders. title: 2027 Toyota Corolla Hatchback Pairs Upgraded Technology with Fun-to-Drive Spirit
summary: PLANO, Texas (July 14, 2026) – Stylish, sporty and packed with smart technology, the 2027 Toyota Corolla Hatchback brings together modern connectivity, athletic styling and a fun-to-drive spirit in a compact package.
body_text: SE Grade Comes Standard With a 7-Inch Digital Gauge Cluster, While the New SE Premium Package Elevates the Experience With a 12.3-Inch Digital Gauge Cluster and a 10.5-Inch Toyota Audio Multimedia System XSE Now Comes Standard with a 12.3-inch Digital Gauge Cluster and a 10.5-inch Toyota Audio Multimedia System Newly Available Toyota Genuine Accessory 18-inch Gloss White Alloy Wheels The 2027 Toyota Corolla Hatchback is Expected to Arrive at Toyota Dealerships This Summer Manufacturer’s Suggested Retail Price, Excluding Dealer Processing and Handling, Starts at $24,780 PLANO, Texas (July 14, 2026) – Stylish, sporty and packed with smart technology, the 2027 Toyota Corolla Hatchback brings together modern connectivity, athletic styling and a fun-to-drive spirit in a compact package. What’s New Updated digital displays help keep drivers connected and informed, while nimble handling and responsive performance help make every mile rewarding. Available in SE and XSE grades, the 2027 Corolla Hatchback continues to offer a sporty, well-equipped lineup with a modern edge. The SE grade now comes standard with a 7-inch digital gauge cluster, while the XSE adds a 12.3-inch digital gauge cluster and a 10.5-inch Toyota Audio Multimedia system as standard equipment. For an even more elevated experience, the new SE Premium Package bundles the 10.5-inch Toyota Audio Multimedia system with the 12.3-inch digital gauge cluster. On the outside, Toyota Genuine accessory 18-inch gloss white alloy wheels are now available*, adding a sharp, sporty accent to the vehicle’s design. Updated exterior color offerings also join the 2027 Corolla Hatchback lineup with Inked, Blueprint and Blueprint with Black Roof expanding the available palette. The 2027 Toyota Corolla Hatchback is expected to arrive at Toyota dealerships this summer. The Manufacturer’s Suggested Retail Price, excluding Dealer Processing and Handling, starts at $24,780. Information on the 2027 Corolla Sedan will be available at a later date. Outstanding Driving Experience Assembled at the Tsutsumi Plant in Aichi, Japan, the 2027 Corolla Hatchback sits on the TNGA-C platform. A solid structure, low center of gravity and highly refined tuning of the MacPherson® strut front and multi-link rear suspensions endow Corolla Hatchback with agile handling, ride comfort and a distinctive driving personality. Under the hood, the Corolla Hatchback is powered by a 2.0-liter Dynamic Force four-cylinder DOHC 16-valve engine. Equipped with Dual Variable Valve Timing with intelligence (VVT-i), it produces 169 horsepower and 151 pound-feet of torque. The Corolla Hatchback also has impressive efficiency, with manufacturer-estimated fuel economy ratings of 32 mpg city, 41 mpg highway and 35 mpg combined on the SE. The Corolla Hatchback features a standard Dynamic Shift continuously variable transmission (CVT) that delivers a distinct performance feel thanks to a physical launch gear for off-the-line acceleration before seamlessly handing off to the CVT’s pulley system. Combined with enhanced sport mode tuning, all grades come standard with paddle shifters that allow drivers to engage 10 pre-set ratios for a sporty driving experience. Drivers can further tailor the Corolla Hatchback’s driving character with NORMAL, ECO and SPORT drive modes. Exterior Corolla Hatchback’s bold look begins with a rounded, muscular physique accented by chiseled character lines and simple, condensed three-dimensional highlights. Combined with 16- or 18-inch alloy tires, including newly available Toyota Genuine accessory 18-inch gloss white alloy wheels, the Hatchback presents an active, well-planted shape and attitude. Slim, aggressive LED headlamps wrap into the front fenders and give Corolla Hatchback a distinct expression. The LED taillamps feature a diffusing inner lens designed to highlight the Hatchback’s stout stance. The XSE features LED fog lights on the front fascia accented by chrome-finished fog bezels. Exterior color options include Blueprint, Inferno, Inked, Classic Silver Metallic, Finish Line Red, Magnetic Gray Metallic, Wind Chill Pearl and Ice Cap. Two-tone black roof color combinations are also available with Blueprint, Classic Silver Metallic, Finish Line Red, Magnetic Gray Metallic and Windchill Pearl. Interior Inside, the Corolla Hatchback has a comfortable and spacious cabin with quality materials, designed with a focus on comfort. In the SE grade, there is a standard 6-way adjustable fabric driver’s seat and a 4-way adjustable front passenger seat. The XSE grade has a standard SofTex®-trimmed 8-way power-adjustable front driver’s seat and a 4-way adjustable front passenger seat, both of which are heated. *Newly available Toyota Genuine accessory 18-inch gloss white alloy wheels require separate purchase of 225/40R18 tires for SE grade. Intuitive Multimedia and Connectivity Technology and convenience remain front and center, with Toyota Safety Sense 3.0 standard across all grades, as well as wireless Apple CarPlay® and Android Auto™ compatibility. The 2027 Corolla Hatchback comes standard with an 8-inch touchscreen featuring Toyota Audio Multimedia, dual Bluetooth® phone connectivity and a six-speaker audio system. Five-year trials of Connected Services are included for Safety Connect**, Service Connect** and Remote Connect**, as well as a 30-day/3 GB trial for Wi-Fi Connect** trial. Additional services, such as Drive Connect**, may be available depending on grade. Visit Toyota Connected Services to learn more. **4G Network-dependent Safety and Convenience Blind Spot Monitor with Rear Cross-Traffic Alert is standard on all grades. It is designed to help detect and warn drivers of vehicles approaching or positioned in adjacent lanes. Rear Cross-Traffic Alert helps detect vehicles approaching from either side while backing out and provides visual and audible warnings. The Toyota Corolla Hatchback comes standard with Toyota Safety Sense 3.0. The suite includes: Pre-Collision System with Pedestrian Detection Full-Speed Range Dynamic Radar Cruise Control Lane Departure Alert with Steering Assist Lane Tracing Assist Road Sign Assist Automatic High Beams Proactive Driving Assist For complete details on Toyota Safety Sense 3.0, please visit Toyota.com/safety-sense . Pricing*** Model # Grade Base MRSP 6272 SE $24,780 6274 XSE $27,875 ***MSRP Excludes Dealer Processing and Handling fee of $1,295. All prices are subject to change. Limited Warranty and ToyotaCare Toyota’s 36-month/36,000 mile basic new-vehicle warranty applies to all components other than normal wear and maintenance items. Additional 60-month warranties cover the powertrain for 60,000 miles and corrosion with no mileage limitation. The Corolla Hatchback also comes standard with ToyotaCare, a maintenance plan that covers normal factory-scheduled service for one year or 10,000 miles, whichever comes first, and 24-hour roadside assistance for two years, unlimited mileage. Toyota directly employs approximately 48,000 people in the U.S. who have contributed to the design, engineering and assembly of more than 36 million cars and trucks at our 11 manufacturing plants. In 2025, Toyota’s plant in North Carolina began to assemble automotive batteries for electrified vehicles. For more information about Toyota, visit www.ToyotaNewsroom.com . title: Puerto Lázaro Cárdenas rompe récord: la carga se dispara 16% en el primer semestre del año
summary: 15.5 millones de toneladas en seis meses y alza del 16%: el Puerto Lázaro Cárdenas se consolida como pieza clave del comercio exterior mexicano en 2026.
body_text: Sign in Welcome! Log into your account Forgot your password? Get help Password recovery Recover your password A password will be e-mailed to you. Puerto Lázaro Cárdenas rompe récord: la carga se dispara 16% en el primer semestre del año El recinto michoacano confirma su lugar entre los grandes del Pacífico mexicano, con cifras que sorprenden en contenedores, autos y minerales. Te contamos cómo logró este repunte y qué hay detrás de los números. Industria 22/07/2026 El Puerto Lázaro Cárdenas atraviesa uno de sus mejores momentos en años recientes. Entre enero y junio, el recinto portuario michoacano movió poco más de 15.5 millones de toneladas de mercancía , una cifra que representa un salto del 16% frente a lo registrado en el mismo lapso de 2025. El dato no solo confirma la recuperación del comercio exterior mexicano por esta vía, sino que posiciona a Lázaro Cárdenas como uno de los puertos con mayor dinamismo del país durante la primera mitad del año. Detrás de este crecimiento hay una combinación de factores: mayor actividad industrial, recuperación en la demanda de minerales, y un repunte notable en el segmento automotriz que, como se detalla más adelante, tuvo un papel protagónico en los resultados del semestre. Movimiento de carga: Contenedores y minerales marcan el paso Al desglosar el tipo de mercancía que pasó por las instalaciones portuarias, la carga contenerizada se llevó la mayor tajada, con casi la mitad del total movilizado (49%). Le siguió de cerca el granel mineral, que concentró poco más de un tercio de las operaciones (36%), reflejo de la fuerte demanda de insumos para la industria siderúrgica y de construcción. La carga general aportó un 5% adicional, mientras que el resto (vehículos, granel agrícola y fluidos petroleros, entre otros) sumó el 10% restante. En el terreno de los contenedores, el puerto movilizó un millón 343 mil 307 TEU’s (esa unidad que equivale a un contenedor estándar de 20 pies), lo que se traduce en un avance del 6% respecto al primer semestre del año anterior. Este indicador es clave porque refleja la salud del comercio exterior contenerizado, uno de los segmentos más competitivos entre los puertos del Pacífico. Un dato que llama la atención es la distribución de este volumen: una cuarta parte correspondió a importaciones, otra cuarta parte a exportaciones, y la mitad, el 50%, se destinó a operaciones de transbordo. Esto confirma algo que analistas del sector marítimo han señalado en los últimos años: Lázaro Cárdenas se ha convertido en un punto de conexión estratégico para embarcaciones que redistribuyen mercancía hacia otros destinos, más allá de ser solamente un puerto de entrada o salida para el mercado mexicano. Esta vocación de “puerto bisagra” le da una ventaja competitiva importante, ya que no depende exclusivamente del consumo interno o de las exportaciones nacionales para mantener su ritmo de operación, sino que también capitaliza el tránsito de mercancía entre distintas rutas comerciales del Pacífico. Transporte de carga: el auge del sector automotriz y el reto de la logística terrestre Si hay un protagonista inesperado en los resultados del semestre, ese es el segmento automotriz. El puerto movilizó 312 mil 649 unidades vehiculares , una cifra considerable que muestra la relevancia de Lázaro Cárdenas como puerta de entrada y salida para la industria automotriz mexicana, uno de los motores manufactureros más importantes del país. De ese total, el 69% correspondió a importaciones de vehículos, lo que confirma el papel del puerto como receptor de unidades provenientes de otros mercados. El 29% fue para exportación, mostrando que también existe un flujo relevante de autos fabricados en México con destino al extranjero, mientras que apenas un 2% se movió como transbordo. Ahora bien, toda esta carga, ya sean contenedores, minerales o automóviles, necesita salir del puerto hacia su destino final, y aquí es donde entra en juego la logística terrestre. De acuerdo con la Administración Portuaria Integral (Asipona) de Lázaro Cárdenas, el 72% de la mercancía salió del recinto por autotransporte, es decir, mediante camiones de carga que distribuyen los productos por carretera hacia distintos puntos del país. El 28% restante se trasladó por ferrocarril, un medio que, aunque representa una porción menor, resulta fundamental para el traslado de grandes volúmenes a largas distancias, particularmente hacia el centro y el bajío del país, donde se concentra buena parte de la industria manufacturera mexicana. Esta proporción entre autotransporte y ferrocarril es un tema que vale la pena seguir de cerca. Mientras el transporte carretero ofrece flexibilidad y rapidez para entregas de corto y mediano alcance, el tren representa una alternativa más eficiente en términos de costo y capacidad para grandes volúmenes, especialmente en un contexto donde la saturación de carreteras y los costos logísticos son una preocupación constante para las empresas que dependen del comercio exterior. Un semestre que marca tendencia Los números del primer semestre dejan claro que Puerto Lázaro Cárdenas no solo está creciendo, sino que lo hace de manera diversificada: contenedores, minerales, automóviles y operaciones de transbordo aportan cada uno una pieza distinta al rompecabezas de su expansión. Si esta tendencia se mantiene durante la segunda mitad del año, el puerto michoacano podría cerrar 2026 con cifras históricas, consolidándose todavía más como una pieza clave en la logística del comercio exterior mexicano y como un punto de conexión imprescindible para el tráfico marítimo del Pacífico. Habrá que estar atentos a los próximos reportes para ver si este ritmo de crecimiento se sostiene, sobre todo en un año donde las dinámicas del comercio internacional siguen mostrando ajustes constantes.
